title: From Soil to Software: Experience from a STEM Workshop on Smart Plant Care and Teachable Machines
problem: Traditional STEM education lacks hands-on, integrated experience with data acquisition, machine learning, and AI. High school students need practical engagement with real-world computing applications.
motivation: STEM education effectiveness improves through hands-on projects. Integrating IoT, data collection, and machine learning in accessible ways can engage students in foundational computing concepts through real-world applications.
method: STEM workshop (3 days, Toledo EXCEL program) combining custom-built IoT sensor system with MakeCode visual programming and Teachable Machine for ML. Students created smart plant care assistant and trained ML classifiers.
key_novelty: Integration of IoT hardware, visual programming, and machine learning in accessible high school workshop; real-world data collection and analysis; hands-on ML training via Teachable Machine.
contributions: Custom-built IoT sensor device for environmental monitoring
Integration of IoT, visual programming, and ML in STEM education
Smart plant care workshop for high school students
Teachable Machine for hands-on ML training
Demonstrated engagement model for computing concepts
Future plans: parallel computing and real-time visualization
limitations: Workshop-based study (limited scale); no quantitative learning outcome metrics provided; single institution; resource requirements for IoT devices.
